title: चतुर्विंशतितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 24 · The kings and the great weapons

summary.en: Gandhari shows Krishna the son of Somadatta, Bhurishravas, killed by Satyaki, and the glittering ornaments of the dead. She tells of Arjuna's great feat and asks how Krishna could allow it, since he had the power to stop the war.
summary.kn: ಗಾಂಧಾರಿ ಸಾತ್ಯಕಿ ಕೊಂದ ಸೋಮದತ್ತನ ಮಗ ಭೂರಿಶ್ರವನನ್ನು, ಹತರ ಹೊಳೆಯುವ ಆಭರಣಗಳನ್ನು ಕೃಷ್ಣನಿಗೆ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತಾಳೆ. ಅರ್ಜುನನ ಮಹಾ ಸಾಹಸ ಹೇಳಿ ಯುದ್ಧ ತಡೆಯುವ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಇದ್ದರೂ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಇದನ್ನು ಹೇಗೆ ಒಪ್ಪಿದನೆಂದು ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾಳೆ.
summary.hi: गान्धारी कृष्ण को सात्यकि द्वारा मारे गए सोमदत्त के पुत्र भूरिश्रवा और मृतकों के चमकते आभूषण दिखाती हैं। वे अर्जुन के महान कर्म की बात करती हैं और पूछती हैं कि युद्ध रोकने की शक्ति होते हुए कृष्ण ने इसे कैसे होने दिया।
summary.te: గాంధారి సాత్యకి చంపిన సోమదత్తుని కుమారుడు భూరిశ్రవుని, హతుల మెరిసే ఆభరణాలను కృష్ణునికి చూపుతుంది. అర్జునుని మహా కార్యాన్ని చెప్పి యుద్ధాన్ని ఆపే శక్తి ఉన్నా కృష్ణుడు దీన్ని ఎలా అనుమతించాడని అడుగుతుంది.
summary.ta: காந்தாரி சாத்யகி கொன்ற சோமதத்தனின் மகன் பூரிசிரவஸையும் மாண்டோரின் மின்னும் நகைகளையும் கண்ணனுக்குக் காட்டுகிறாள். அர்ஜுனனின் பெருஞ்செயலைக் கூறி, போரைத் தடுக்கும் ஆற்றல் இருந்தும் கண்ணன் ஏன் அனுமதித்தார் என்று கேட்கிறாள்.
summary.ml: സാത്യകി വധിച്ച സോമദത്തന്റെ പുത്രൻ ഭൂരിശ്രവസ്സിനെയും, മരിച്ചവരുടെ തിളങ്ങുന്ന ആഭരണങ്ങളെയും ഗാന്ധാരി കൃഷ്ണനെ കാണിക്കുന്നു. അർജുനന്റെ മഹത്തായ വിരുതിനെക്കുറിച്ച് പറയുന്ന അവൾ, യുദ്ധം തടയാൻ ശക്തിയുണ്ടായിട്ടും അത് എങ്ങനെ അനുവദിച്ചുവെന്ന് കൃഷ്ണനോട് ചോദിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 11.24; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Apr 17 2017

verses.text: गान्धार्युवाच

meaning.en: Gandhari said:

verses.text:
सोमदत्तसुतं पश्य युयुधानेन पातितम् ।
वितुद्यमानं विहगैर्बहुभिर्माधवान्तिके ॥

meaning.en: Look at Somadatta's son, felled by Yuyudhana and torn by many birds, here near you, Madhava.

verses.text:
पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः सोमदत्तो जनार्दन ।
युयुधानं महेष्वासं गर्हयन्निव दृश्यते ॥

meaning.en: Janardana, Somadatta, burning with grief for his son, appears to be reproaching the great archer Yuyudhana.

verses.text:
असौ तु भूरिश्रवसो माता शोकपरिप्लुता ।
आश्वासयति भर्तारं सोमदत्तमनिन्दिता ॥

meaning.en: And here is Bhurishravas's mother, blameless, flooded with grief, comforting her husband Somadatta.

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या नेदं महाराज दारुणं भरतक्षयम् ।
कुरुसंक्रन्दनं घोरं युगान्तमनुपश्यसि ॥

meaning.en: By good fortune, great king, you do not see this cruel destruction of the Bharatas, the dreadful wailing of the Kurus like the end of an age.

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या यूपध्वजं वीरं पुत्रं भूरिसहस्रदम् ।
अनेकक्रतुयज्वानं निहतं नाद्य पश्यसि ॥

meaning.en: By good fortune you do not see today your hero son, with the sacrificial post as his banner, who gave thousands of gifts and performed many sacrifices, slain.

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या स्नुषाणामाक्रन्दे घोरं विलपितं बहु ।
न शृणोषि महाराज सारसीनामिवार्णवे ॥

meaning.en: By good fortune, great king, you do not hear the terrible, many-voiced lament of your daughters-in-law, like the cries of cranes by the sea.

verses.text:
एकवस्त्रानुसंवीताः प्रकीर्णासितमूर्धजाः ।
स्नुषास्ते परिधावन्ति हतापत्या हतेश्वराः ॥

meaning.en: Wearing a single garment, with loose black hair, your daughters-in-law, their children and lords dead, run about.

verses.text:
श्वापदैर्भक्ष्यमाणं त्वमहो दिष्ट्या न पश्यसि ।
छिन्नबाहुं नरव्याघ्रमर्जुनेन निपातितम् ॥

meaning.en: By good fortune you do not see the tiger among men, his arm cut off by Arjuna, being devoured by beasts.

verses.text:
शलं विनिहतं संख्ये भूरिश्रवसमेव च ।
स्नुषाश्च विधवाः सर्वा दिष्ट्या नाद्येह पश्यसि ॥

meaning.en: By good fortune you do not see here today Shala slain in battle, and Bhurishravas, and all these widowed daughters-in-law.

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या तत्काञ्चनं छत्रं यूपकेतोर्महात्मनः ।
विनिकीर्णं रथोपस्थे सौमदत्तेर्न पश्यसि ॥

meaning.en: By good fortune you do not see the golden umbrella of the great-souled one with the sacrificial post banner, scattered on the chariot-seat of Somadatta's son.

verses.text:
अमूस्तु भूरिश्रवसो भार्याः सात्यकिना हतम् ।
परिवार्यानुशोचन्ति भर्तारमसितेक्षणाः ॥

meaning.en: And these wives of Bhurishravas, dark-eyed, surround their husband, who was killed by Satyaki, and mourn him.

verses.text:
एता विलप्य बहुलं भर्तृशोकेन कर्शिताः ।
पतन्त्यभिमुखा भूमौ कृपणं बत केशव ॥

meaning.en: Keshava, these women, wasted with grief for their husband, having wept much, fall face down on the ground, pitiably.

verses.text:
बीभत्सुरतिबीभत्सं कर्मेदमकरोत्कथम् ।
प्रमत्तस्य यदच्छैत्सीद्बाहुं शूरस्य यज्वनः ॥

meaning.en: How did Bibhatsu do this most hideous deed, that he cut off the arm of the heroic sacrificer while he was heedless?

verses.text:
ततः पापतरं कर्म कृतवानपि सात्यकिः ।
यस्मात्प्रायोपविष्टस्य प्राहार्षीत्संशितात्मनः ॥

meaning.en: Yet Satyaki did a still worse deed, in that he struck the disciplined man who sat fasting until death.

verses.text:
एको द्वाभ्यां हतः शेषे त्वमधर्मेण धार्मिकः ।
इति यूपध्वजस्यैताः स्त्रियः क्रोशन्ति माधव ॥

meaning.en: "You, the righteous man, alone, were killed by two, unfairly." So these women of the one with the sacrificial post as banner cry out, Madhava.

verses.text:
भार्या यूपध्वजस्यैषा करसंमितमध्यमा ।
कृत्वोत्सङ्गे भुजं भर्तुः कृपणं पर्यदेवयत् ॥

meaning.en: Here is the wife of the one with the sacrificial post banner, her waist small enough to be held in a hand, who has laid her husband's arm on her lap and laments piteously:

verses.text:
अयं स रशनोत्कर्षी पीनस्तनविमर्दनः ।
नाभ्यूरुजघनस्पर्शी नीवीविस्रंसनः करः ॥

meaning.en: "This is the hand that pulled at the girdle, pressed full breasts, touched navel, thighs and hips, and loosened the waistband.

verses.text:
वासुदेवस्य सांनिध्ये पार्थेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।
युध्यतः समरेऽन्येन प्रमत्तस्य निपातितः ॥

meaning.en: "In Vasudeva's presence, when you were fighting another and heedless, you were felled by Partha of untiring deeds.

verses.text:
किं नु वक्ष्यसि संसत्सु कथासु च जनार्दन ।
अर्जुनस्य महत्कर्म स्वयं वा स किरीटवान् ॥

meaning.en: "What will you say, Janardana, in assemblies and conversations about Arjuna's great deed, or will the crowned one say it himself?"

verses.text:
इत्येवं गर्हयित्वैषा तूष्णीमास्ते वराङ्गना ।
तामेतामनुशोचन्ति सपत्न्यः स्वामिव स्नुषाम् ॥

meaning.en: Having thus reproached, the fair woman remains silent, and her co-wives mourn her as if she were their own daughter-in-law.

verses.text:
गान्धारराजः शकुनिर्बलवान्सत्यविक्रमः ।
निहतः सहदेवेन भागिनेयेन मातुलः ॥

meaning.en: The king of Gandhara, Shakuni, strong and truly valiant, was killed by Sahadeva, his sister's son, though he was his uncle.

verses.text:
यः पुरा हेमदण्डाभ्यां व्यजनाभ्यां स्म वीज्यते ।
स एष पक्षिभिः पक्षैः शयान उपवीज्यते ॥

meaning.en: He who once was fanned with two golden-handled fans now lies and is fanned by birds with their wings.

verses.text:
यः स्म रूपाणि कुरुते शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।
तस्य मायाविनो माया दग्धाः पाण्डवतेजसा ॥

meaning.en: He who made forms in hundreds and thousands, that trickster's tricks have been burned up by the Pandavas' might.

verses.text:
मायया निकृतिप्रज्ञो जितवान्यो युधिष्ठिरम् ।
सभायां विपुलं राज्यं स पुनर्जीवितं जितः ॥

meaning.en: He who with a cheat's cunning won from Yudhishthira the vast kingdom in the assembly has now lost his own life.

verses.text:
शकुन्ताः शकुनिं कृष्ण समन्तात्पर्युपासते ।
कितवं मम पुत्राणां विनाशायोपशिक्षितम् ॥

meaning.en: Krishna, birds sit all around Shakuni, the gambler trained for the destruction of my sons.

verses.text:
एतेनैतन्महद्वैरं प्रसक्तं पाण्डवैः सह ।
वधाय मम पुत्राणामात्मनः सगणस्य च ॥

meaning.en: He started this great enmity with the Pandavas, for the killing of my sons and of himself with his followers.

verses.text:
यथैव मम पुत्राणां लोकाः शस्त्रजिताः प्रभो ।
एवमस्यापि दुर्बुद्धेर्लोकाः शस्त्रेण वै जिताः ॥

meaning.en: Lord, just as my sons' worlds were won by weapons, so the worlds of this ill-minded man were won by weapons.

verses.text:
कथं च नायं तत्रापि पुत्रान्मे भ्रातृभिः सह ।
विरोधयेदृजुप्रज्ञाननृजुर्मधुसूदन ॥

meaning.en: Madhusudana, how can this crooked man not, even there, set against one another my honest sons and their brothers?
